claim: Deficiencies the auditor finds: "Reported in writing to management and the audit committee" with attestation; "Unchanged" without.
evidence: With attestation, three rules apply. AS 2201.78: "communicate, in writing, to management and the audit committee all material weaknesses". AS 2201.80: significant deficiencies "in writing, to the audit committee". AS 2201.81: "communicate to management, in writing, all deficiencies ... and inform the audit committee". Without attestation, AS 1305.04 governs: "communicate in writing to management and the audit committee all significant deficiencies and material weaknesses". AS 1305.07: lesser deficiencies "may" be reported. AS 1305.08: the auditor "should not report in writing that no significant deficiencies were discovered". Lesser deficiencies are therefore no longer required to be reported, and fewer will be found because fewer controls are tested. https://pcaobus.org/Standards/Auditing/Pages/AS1305.aspx
fix: With: "Material weaknesses in writing to management and the audit committee; significant deficiencies in writing to the audit committee; all other deficiencies in writing to management (AS 2201.78-.81)". Without: "Significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in writing to management and the audit committee; lesser deficiencies at the auditor's discretion (AS 1305.04, .07)".
why: Corrected in v2 from the primary source.

claim: A material weakness management has not reported: the auditor says so in its report (with attestation); without it, it goes to management and the audit committee "to weigh in management's assessment".

Without: AS 1305.04 requires written communication "prior to the issuance of the auditor's report on the financial statements". "To weigh in management's assessment" is an inference; AS 1305 does not say it. Management stays bound by the SOX 302 certification. Item 601(b)(31) ¶5 (Rules 13a-14/15d-14): officers "have disclosed ... to the registrant's auditors and the audit committee ... All significant deficiencies and material weaknesses in the design or operation of internal control over financial reporting". https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/section-229.601

claim: Banks stay subject to the FDIC's attestation rule, "which since January 1, 2026 applies at $5 billion of assets or more".
evidence: FDIC final rule, 90 FR 55789 (Dec. 4, 2025), https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/04/2025-21914: "The final rule is effective January 1, 2026." It "raises ... the ICFR asset threshold from $1 billion to $5 billion". 12 CFR 363.2(b)(3) and 363.3(b) (eCFR current to 10/06/2026): management's assessment and the auditor's attestation apply to "each insured depository institution with total assets of $5 billion, as adjusted ... in accordance with 12 CFR 314.1, or more at the beginning of the institution's fiscal year." Both thresholds are $5bn. The rule applies to the insured bank, not the SEC-registered holding company. §363.1(b)(2): a holding company may satisfy it if comparable services are provided at holding-company level, the bank is at least 75% of holding-company assets, and the bank has under $5bn of assets or a CAMELS rating of 1 or 2. Banks can also take the relief for fiscal 2025 ("need not comply with the ... requirements in effect as of December 31, 2025").
fix: p. 8: "Bank holding companies are counted in the 1,596, but their insured banks remain under the FDIC's Part 363, which from January 1, 2026 requires a management assessment and an auditor's attestation on internal control at each insured depository institution with $5 billion or more of total assets at the start of its fiscal year, a threshold now indexed to inflation. The requirement can be met at holding-company level, so a holding company that drops its Section 404(b) attestation may still need one for its bank." p. 16 item 3: "Insured banks with $5 billion or more of total assets stay under the FDIC's Part 363 attestation, whatever the holding company's filer status."
why: Corrected in v2 from the primary source.
